name: Plain to See
tagline: You take a yes more seriously than a no.
epigraph: Two countries, two whiskies, both often called rye. In one, the rye is usually a little.
glassware: small tumbler (about 200 ml), chilled in the freezer, no ice

open_items: Tamarind water is the drink's one variable: its acid and sugar are the middle of the tamarind card's range (El-Siddig et al. 2006), unsourced for any given block. The dose is sensitive (5 ml reads OUT low and 10 ml OUT high at the card's middle), so the recipe gives three stops (1, 1½, 2 tsp) for very sour, middling and mild blocks; each is proven at its end of the range. The taste cue that picks the stop is Tomás's craft call, unsourced.
Canadian whisky at 40% is Oxford's legal floor (pdf 2146); real bottlings may run higher, swept to 45%: in range.

Hester struck her own plan-row wording in r4: the Matrix lists tamarind as going with both grains, not as a flavour both grains share; the reading, Notes, Checks and anchors all now say "goes with both grains".
The plan row cited Oxford JACKSON as pdf 1090–1091; the entry is pdf 1091–1092 (Hester's correction, C1 on the card).
